Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1032 AM EDT Wed Jul 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Confidence is slowly increasing that the highest shower and 
thunderstorm chances will be this afternoon and evening across
southern Maryland.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A few strong to severe thunderstorms are possible from
  central Virginia to southern Maryland this afternoon. 
  
- 2) Below average temperatures and mainly dry conditions are
  expected Thursday through Saturday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A few strong to severe thunderstorms are
possible from central Virginia to southern Maryland this 
afternoon.

As of 10 AM, radar imagery shows showers and thunderstorms 
passing just to the south of the area across southeastern 
Virginia. Clouds and a few showers on the northwestern fringe of
that activity have made it into St. Mary's County. Further 
north, skies remain mostly sunny across the majority of the 
forecast area. 

A prefrontal trough will switch winds to westerly through much
of the day before northerly winds bring the true airmass change
tonight. The cold front likely overtakes the trough at some
point but will temporarily stall this afternoon, likely
extending across central Virginia to southern Maryland. Dew
points will remain in the 70s in this area, supporting some
instability to go along with the wind shear provided by the
upper trough. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms
are forecast along and southeast of the front, although there 
remains some uncertainty in coverage and intensity. Given the 
shear in place, there is some potential for severe 
thunderstorms, with damaging winds being the primary threat. 
Thunderstorms may also be repetitive along the slow moving 
front, but the expected fast individual storm motions will 
likely preclude any flood threat.

The front will drop south of the area this evening, but an area
of low pressure may ride along it. This could result in
additional showers spreading across central Virginia and
southern Maryland through the night.

In terms of temperatures, highs today will be in the 70s to
lower 80s west of I-81 and mid to upper 80s to the east.
Lows tonight will drop into the 50s and 60s, and some of the
sheltered high elevation valleys could reach the 40s.
 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Below average temperatures and mainly dry
conditions are expected Thursday through Saturday.

A sprawling area of high pressure will build to our north for 
Thursday and Friday, before shifting off the New England 
Coastline on Saturday. Northerly flow ahead of the approaching 
high will advect a much cooler and drier airmass into the region
for Thursday. Well below normal temperatures and dewpoints are 
forecast for late July, with high temperatures only in the upper
70s/low 80s. Dewpoints in the 50s will also make it feel much 
less humid than is typical for July. Mostly sunny skies will 
accompany the well below normal temperatures/dewpoints. 
Temperatures will stay well below normal for Friday and Saturday
within easterly flow. Some moisture could be drawn northward
from the stalled frontal zone across the southeastern states
during this time. The current forecast has some low rain chances
both days, mainly in southern portions of the CWA and along the
Allegheny Mountains.

Both temperatures and dewpoints begin to rise again on Sunday 
as flow turns southerly, with highs in the mid to upper 80s and 
dewpoints in the 60s. The return of higher dewpoint air should 
lead to slightly greater chances for afternoon/evening showers 
and thunderstorms, but most locations will likely still stay 
dry.

Forecast confidence decreases substantially by Monday and Tuesday, 
but chances for showers and thunderstorms may further increase as 
multiple shortwave disturbances move through in northwesterly flow 
aloft. Depending on how the forecast details evolve, there could be 
a conditional threat for severe thunderstorms on either Monday or 
Tuesday.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
A cold front will slowly move southward across the area today. 
Some showers and thunderstorms may form ahead of the front this 
afternoon, potentially affecting CHO and DCA. The greatest 
coverage may be just to the south though. A wave of low pressure
may ride along the front this evening and could push some 
additional showers toward CHO and DCA, but most of the lower 
ceilings will likely remain to the south. Winds will turn 
northerly this evening.

Prevailing VFR condtions are expected most of the time between
Thursday through Sunday. There may be some lower ceilings at 
times this weekend in onshore flow, but confidence is low. Winds
will generally be out of the north on Thursday, east on Friday,
and southeast on Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory level winds continue to linger this morning
across across the Lower Tidal Potomac and Central Bay. Strong 
to perhaps severe thunderstorms may develop ahead of a cold 
front this afternoon and evening across mainly southern 
Maryland.

A pressure surge and accompanying shift to northerly winds will
push across the waters this evening. Small Craft Advisories have
been issued for tonight into Thursday morning along the bay.

Thereafter, sub-SCA level winds are expected Thursday afternoon
through Sunday. Winds will generally be out of the north on 
Thursday, east on Friday, and southeast on Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Anomalies remain between 0.5-1 foot this morning. Havre de 
Grace may approach minor flood stage this morning but should 
remain below. Water levels will drop as a cold front passes 
later today.
